en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qing of Touzi in Shu Prefecture:

Long ago, within the Yangshan mountains, a wooden man sat alone and a stone maiden conceived a child; yet for many years it was not brought forth. Before the mountain, auspicious grasses grow—whom shall they entrust to tend them?
By the ridge, a mud ox wanders—who can restrain or release it? Upon the dais of the King of Emptiness, the axle of the chariot is about to...
"Crush! At the ferry crossing of the ancient Buddhas, the gunwales were about to break. There was only a half-worn leather sandal and a seamless cotton robe presented face-to-face at that time;
yet, in the end, no one could take it up. The moonlight shines in perfect clarity, sighing deeply with knitted brows.
He carried it back to the cave of Jingu, entrusting it to the Old Man of White Clouds. Thus, the golden cock brooded its eggs and the vermilion phoenix was born."
The fledglings emerge; the jade trees bloom with flowers and the peaches of immortality bear fruit. It truly causes the mountains and rivers to tremble and the great earth to surge.
How remarkably fresh it is! It is also a most wondrous marvel. From this point on, the old shop shall reopen in the oil-selling market;
the incense burner in the ancient temple shall rise again with auspicious smoke. The melodies of the Hu family’s songs shall soar into the blue heavens, inscribed upon the void.
Within the bamboo flute of Kongzi, it is unknown who will lend an ear. May this be transmitted to all quarters, each person carefully preserving and upholding it.
When one encounters a connoisseur, let the assembly blow and sing it together.
This preface was written on the full moon day of the fourth month in the seventh year of the Yuanfeng era by Li Yuanchong of Longman.

The Recorded Sayings of Master Touzi Qing, Volume One.
Recorded Sayings of Master Qing of Mount Touzi in Shuzhou, while Residing at Haihui Chan Monastery in Baiyunshan.
(Compiled by the Dharma-transmitting Bhikṣu Zizhao, while [Master Qing] was residing at Jinyin Chan Monastery in the Northern Ward of the Capital.)
On the day the Master opened the hall, the great assembly had gathered. The County Magistrate, the Vice Prefect, presented the petition to the Master.
Upon receiving it, the Master said: "If the mind is free from affairs, the myriad dharmas do not arise; if the intent is cut off from the subtle and profound, how could even a speck of dust stand?
He then held up the petition and asked: "Tell me, from where did this come? If you can say, then the stone man will dance his sleeves and join in the celebration."
"Peace and tranquility. If you cannot say it, then I ask the *vinaya-dhara* (rectifier) to explain it for the sake of the assembly.
Having finished reciting the memorial, the Master pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "Great assembly, all the sages of the past, upon reaching this point, let go from emptiness.
I, however, am not like this; here, I ascend higher with every step. Why? Because 'if one wishes to exhaust the view across a thousand li, one must climb even higher.'"

Upon reaching the first floor, he ascended the seat. Elder Taiping offered incense to the Master. The Master accepted it and said: "This single portion of incense is offered to extend the sacred longevity of the current Emperor.
We respectfully pray that Your Majesty’s life may endure as long as heaven and earth, and as vast as the sun and moon."
With pure clarity, the eight directions sing the wind of Yao and Shun; from the four frontiers, all offer congratulations on the transformation of Yu and Tang.
(Having offered the incense for the lay officials: Does the assembly know the origin of this single portion of incense? It was not produced by heaven and earth, nor was it formed by yin and yang.
Before the time of Wei-yin, it did not fall into any rank; after the Lamp of Dīpaṃkara, it was transmitted through the Seven Buddhas, reaching down to Caoxi where it was divided.
I have sent this to Daxia. When I was at Mount Fushan at the beginning of the Zhi-ping era, I received the transmission from the hand of Chan Master Yuanjian of Fushan;
he entrusted me with his lineage. The verse was composed by Wei Zhengming. My late master’s instruction said: "Continue my lineage and perpetuate the tradition of Dayang.
Although I did not personally know Chan Master Dayang, I relied on Fushan’s method of discerning people to recognize him as my successor. It is thus.
Furthermore, not violating the grace of the Dharma-entrustment and final instructions of Chan Master Fushan Yuanjian, he respectfully acted on behalf of Master Ming’an of Dayang Mountain in Yingzhou.
Why? Because parents and all Buddhas are not one’s true kin; it is the Dharma that is one’s true kin. Thereupon, he sat cross-legged.
Elder Shanggu struck the gavel and said: "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary principle. The Master then—
He said, "O Great Assembly! Do you still know that [this] has already fallen into the secondary meaning? If it were the primary meaning, how would you observe it?
Reaching this point, even if the entire bodies of the patriarchs and Buddhas were eyes, there would be no door through which to see.

In the space of a single breath of a patch-robed monk, there are a thousand births and ten thousand kalpas. The six patriarchs knit their brows; past and present stand upside down. This causes [Vimalakīrti] to remain silent in his room at Mākandika."

Exhausted. Vimalakīrti remained silent at Vaiśālī; for nine years at Shaoshi, Huineng crossed the Huangmei River by night. If one were to act according to the full implementation of the Dharma, one must simply tread upon the thorns of the heavens.
This is because the transformation of the prefecture descends clearly and the light of the district illuminates the administration.

It is due to the distant cause of inheriting the Buddha’s entrustment and the immediate protection of the path of flourishing prosperity. Today, for the sake of the nation, the hall is opened and the Dharma is expounded, in order to offer a supreme response.

The Imperial Household, with trembling sincerity, prays with single-minded devotion. Among the assembly, there was one who had long carried the lineage of his ancestors and accumulated the wearing of seals and cases;
disregarding the height of Mount Dayu, he immediately requested to cut through the clouds to meet him. At that time, a monk asked: "Whose song does the Master sing?
Whom does the patriarchal wind succeed? The Master said: "Before the Nameless One, a single arrow pierces through two mountains."
The monk asked, "What is the matter that is transmitted? The Master said, "It is entirely because of the moon over Huai that the spring of Yingyang is illuminated.
The monk asked, "If that is so, then one enters the water and sees the tall man. The Master said, "One knows only that the jade of Jing is extraordinary;
how can one discern the heart of King Chu? He then struck the meditation seat once with his whisk. A monk asked, "In the past, at the Many Sons Stupa..."
[The student] had previously heard the prediction of his enlightenment. This morning, beneath the White Cloud Peak, he wished to hear the sound of the tide.

The Master said: "A purple phoenix dances before the steps; a golden rooster crows facing the sun. [The student] further asked: "If that is so, then the Five Mountains stand firm as the earth's center, and the hundred valleys flow far toward the capital.
The Master said: "Beyond the clouds, a thousand peaks are emerald; the sound of the stream is cold with a single drop. [The student] further asked: "A single sheet of white clouds..."
"The world is vast and expansive; there is nowhere under heaven where its shade does not descend. The Master said, "The dragon roars in the green ravine; the mist honors the frosty flowers.
A monk asked, "Yesterday I left Taiping in Shu Prefecture, and today I have arrived at Baiyun Haihui. What is the Immovable Honored One?"
The Master said, "White clouds come and go beyond the green mountains; the cold pines atop the ridge stand high with the moon.

The monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, one does not leave this place yet reaches everywhere else. The Master said, "Do not ask about the road ahead; it is deep where the solitary monkey cries. The monk bowed.
The Master let out a sigh and asked, "Is there anyone else who wishes to speak? When there was no response, he said, "If there is none, we shall both rest."

It is so. Why? If we discuss this matter, how could it be considered a transcendence of the world merely by ascending the Dharma seat, arranging the ranks of the worthy and the eminent, or engaging in the dialogue of questioner and respondent?
Furthermore, the thousand worthies have closed their mouths and the ten thousand sages have ceased speaking;

the Buddhas and Patriarchs of past and present have no means to clear the matter, and the Three Baskets and Five Vehicles offer no further instruction. Nevertheless, although this is so, one must not simply let the bowstring snap.
The arrows have all been spent. Thus it is said: "A thousand peaks lock in color; ten thousand trees congeal in cold.
The moon shines upon ancient crags as wind arises; clouds part on all four sides of the secluded caverns. The dragon roars from withered wood; the phoenix warbles in the crimson heavens.

The stone ox bellows, severing the long sky; the wooden horse neighs, opening the golden gates. Spiritual sprouts compete to flourish; auspicious grasses vie for spring. Sun and moon shine together. A thousand—
The Yangtze River flows together with the rain. To attain such a state is still merely a matter on the periphery of transcending the world; it remains caught within the present moment.

Distinguished ones, how can you avoid falling into the present moment? After a long silence, he said: "The path to the Ten-Thousand-Year Rock is locked by a thousand clouds; a single range of green mountains is sealed at midnight.
He struck the gavel and said: "Contemplate closely the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma of the Dharma-King is thus. Then he descended from the seat.
The Master was ascending the seat after receiving his certificate at Taiping. A monk asked: "When the Buddhas do not appear in the world, how is this one phrase proclaimed?
When the Buddhas have already appeared in the world, to whom is this one phrase shown? The Master said: "The stone man walks through the snow; the pure wind fills [the ten directions]."

[The Master] took his seat. [The monk] stepped forward and said, "The entire assembly is straining their ears; today, everyone has attained true knowledge. The Master said, "Disciple, please lower your voice.
The monk said, "Clouds rise to the heavens, and rain moistens the great thousandfold world. How is it, World-Honored One, regarding your appearance in this world? The Master said:

"The bright moon stretches across the monasteries; the green mountains draw near the white clouds. The monk continued, "A single incense stick of agalloch and sandalwood burns; its fragrance is heard far and wide.
The Master said, "At the foot of Chicken Peak Rock, the dhūta is laughing to death. The monk prostrated himself. The Master asked, "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question?
If there is none, we both gain the advantage. Why? If one discusses this matter, it is like a phoenix soaring to the heavens—"
Its traces remain; when a wild goat hangs from a horn, how can one seek its tracks? When the golden dragon does not dwell in the cold pool, how could the jade hare rest within the shadow of the moon?
Should host and guest still stand apart, one must shake the head beyond the Road of Voice-Sound.

When questions and answers are presented, they are further raised as a chant alongside the Mysterious Path. If one can do so, one is still only halfway there; furthermore, one must remain steadfast...
[The Master] looked at him with his eyes. [The formal words of dismissal are not recorded.

On the following night, during the *xiaocan* (small session), a monk asked: "I have heard that Master Ming'an’s verse says: 'The grass on the peak of Mount Yangguang—rely on you to wait for its price to be set.
Tonight, the Cloth Bag has been opened; I pray the Master will grant us an instruction. The Master said: "Auspicious grass reaches to the heavens in its splendor."
"The reeds and flowers face the bright moon. The student said, "I do not yet understand; I ask the Master to point it out again.
The Master said, "Go back down to the crags first, and wait until the time the moon is bright. The student said, "If that is so, then wild fires cannot burn them away;
when the spring wind blows, they grow once more. The Master said, "The true command has already been issued. Next, a monk held up his sitting cloth and said, "Mañjuśrī’s sword is here."
[The Master] said, "If you open your mouth and move your tongue, you will lose your body and forfeit your life. Please, Master, answer my question. The Master struck the meditation seat once.
[The monk] stepped forward and said, "Truly a masterful hand! The Master said, "Do not misunderstand. The Master then said, "Last night, when the bell rang—"
"All you practitioners have come here. When the bell sounds tonight, will you come again? What business do you have? The moon shines upon the secluded chamber, cold;

the stars divide, each orbiting the North Star in its own way. "If this were Tao Yuanming, he would knit his brows and turn back. After a long silence, he said: "Tonight, I shall not cause you all to knit your brows. Why?
Because my heart bears no grudge against others, and my face shows no shame. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall upon entering the monastery, a monk asked: "In the past, when the Elder Sudatta invited the Buddha to preach the Dharma, he spread gold beneath his feet.
Today, as you, Master, appear in the world, what extraordinary excellence do you possess? The Master said: "Today the frost is heavy. The monk pressed further:
"If that is so, then auspicious clouds arise beyond the railing, and auspicious vapors gather before the steps. The Master said: "The stream water is green with mist; the pine trees are..."
Daiyue Gao asked, "Tell me, is the World-Honored One’s appearance in the world the same as or different from your Reverence’s appearance in the world?
The Master said, "Disciple, you must determine this for yourself. Gao replied, "A master of the school, the eyes of the heavens and the human realm.
The Master said, "A clear-eyed monk cannot be deceived by even a single point. The Master then said, "Great assembly, beneath the White Cloud Rock is the home of the ancient Buddha."
The Wind. This is the livelihood of the man of the Way before the peaks of the azure crags: wind arises on the ancient ridges, and the moon shines upon the front valley.
The sound of pines mingles with the resonance of emerald bamboos; flowing water joins the mountain clouds in a shared radiance. When the antelope hangs its horns, one searches for east and west;
when the gates of the pavilion open, one rejoices at meeting. "Great assembly, there is no doubt that you have met me, but do you recognize me? After a long silence, he said:
Who would have known that beneath this scholar’s cap was none other than the person of former times? [He] descended from his seat.

On the following day, he ascended the hall to express his gratitude to the various administrators: At Baiyun, the dawn breaks over Mount Baiyun; Green bamboos and pine trees, where the bird-path is tranquil.
Last night the monkeys cried out toward the western ridge; This morning, the misty clouds linger idly within the Patriarch’s Hall.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a fish fleeing into the deep abyss—it inevitably attracts the fisherman. It is like jade buried in the Jing Valley—how could it resist those who seek it?
Thus, the amputation of his feet at the city of Chu and the misty waters of the Wei River were both caused by failing to maintain one's ordinary state, leading to such consequences as these.
On this day, white clouds fill the valley and green waters float with mist; auspicious birds startle at dawn and the mountain light dazzles the eyes."

To act without partiality in all matters—what could be improper? Nevertheless, even so, you must further be able to shade the sun with handless hands and catch fish without touching the pole. [Descend from the seat.]

On the Winter Solstice, the Master ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered and settled, he struck once with his staff. After a long silence, he said: "The first yang has arisen. Therefore it is said:
'Outside the path of the ancient Buddhas, the thousand sages do not travel. The patriarchs transmitted the fragrance [of the Dharma], vesting the *kāṣāya* to establish their credibility.
Since the time of Caoxi, the lineages have dispersed and branched out; the various masters each established themselves within a single school, and their transmissions have been passed down together."
To bring this matter to light: on this day, as the first yang reaches its seasonal limit, all things harbor their vital spirits.

A piercing wind blows open the blossoms upon Chicken Rock; a jade hare pushes through the azure void. The dragon gives birth to its offspring; the tiger cradles the qilin. Spiritual sprouts bear radiance amidst the snow;
auspicious grasses spread across the earth in harmony with the clouds. Although it is thus, tell me: where does the wondrous point lie prior to the body?
"How would you say it? After a long silence, he said: "Once the single breath has given rise to heaven and earth, where can the myriad spirits fail to express their gratitude for this impartiality?
Having stood for a long time, he prostrated himself before the assembly; may you all be well and cherished.

Master Xie Hua ascends the hall: "The green peaks stretch across the void, and white clouds drift in their own distinct way. The numinous sprout stands alone in its excellence; how could profuse weeds grow there?

Where the golden cock crows, the moon has fallen at the third watch; when the jade hare sleeps, the sun’s wheel is at midday. In the imperial garden of the jade forest, withered trees welcome the spring;
upon the jeweled palace, moss grows as songs of joy reach ten thousand miles. Although it is thus, tell me: what is the response?
"How do you express the single phrase 'responding to the season'? After a long silence, he said: "In the deep snow of last night, several branches have blossomed at dawn.

Addressing the alms-collectors, he ascended the hall and said: "With pure resolve, they carry their staffs across distant peaks; whether high or low, they proceed with ease in their quest for alms along the way."
A person of middle capacity asks about the matter of White Clouds. He points distantly toward the thousands of layers of green mountains.

Standing for a long time, take care of yourselves. Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Imperial Birthday: Heaven drapes down jade dew; the earth surges forth auspicious clouds. A thousand rivers are clear, and ten-thousand acres of misty waves stretch out.

From the four frontiers, congratulations are offered upon the wind of Yao and the transformation of Shun. Mountains connect with the azure heavens; trees stir up a pure breeze. The flowers of the Jasper Forest bloom amidst the precious groves.
In the imperial willow groves by the pond, orioles sing within the Jade Garden; the stars divide the Purple Pavilion, and the hours encircle the Celestial Wheel.

The myriad states celebrate the occasion of the Sage’s birth, and the ten thousand nations pray for the longevity of the Southern Mountain. Truly, the mountains and rivers gather their splendors, and the seas and peaks manifest their radiance.
The golden cock vibrates its cry beyond the heavens; the jade throne receives the dignity of a thousand springs. O virtuous ones, at such a time as this, tell me:
how do you express the single phrase of the perfect union between sovereign and minister? After a long silence, he said: "When the Way prevails, sovereign and minister purify the universe;
when times are prosperous, all join in celebrating the era of Shun and Yao."

The Master ascended the seat at Ganlu and said: "O Great Assembly! The ancestral peaks rise in a thousand crags; the lineage flows in ten thousand streams. Verdant clouds lock high upon the long pines;
the bright moon shines universally over the myriad waters. Spring brings life to the southern bank; flowers bloom on the eastern branches.
The golden crow and the jade hare share their radiance; the wooden horse chases the stone ox as they run side by side. The snow has melted from Shaolin; life springs forth from the withered tree."
Fragrance! The peaks of Chicken Peak are sealed; fragrant clouds spread across the fields. O virtuous ones, tell me: how do you express that single phrase before the Seamless Stūpa?
After a long silence, he said: "Where the Milky Way is full, the handle of the Dipper hangs high."珍重 (Take care).
Ascending the hall, he said: "The clouds unroll over the myriad peaks; the green mountains stand out in distant splendor. The green vines are thick with mist; dewdrops fall like bright pearls.

Where the white monkeys cry, the moon faces the eaves; when the jade hare sleeps, the sun’s wheel is at its zenith. Now tell me, how do you speak that single phrase which does not err regarding light or darkness?
After a long silence, he said: "Clouds hide the peaks for a thousand li; rain nourishes the eternal rocks. He descended from the seat.

Seated on the high seat, he ascended the hall and said: "Silence sinks one into the realm of darkness; speech falls into a deep pit. To attempt to grasp it is to create a vast distance between heaven and earth;
to abandon it is to wander through a thousand lives and ten thousand kalpas. The vast waves surge and the white billows overflow the heavens—where does the bright pearl that tames the sea lie?"
[The Master] strikes the palm [of his hand]. He suddenly picks up his staff, strikes it once, and says, "All shattered!
Then he descends from the seat. Addressing the fundraising host as he enters the hall, he says: "The journey of one hundred thousand li from the West involved traversing many mountains and rivers.

For nine years, the two states of Wei and Liang waited for the opportune moment. Thus, the mind-seal of the Tathāgata remains present, and the robe and bowl of Caoxi are still arrayed here. The temple has been established."

In this monastery, a sanctuary for the Brahma-realm, the propagation of the Great Doctrine relies upon the pure assembly from the four quarters. Before the Wheel of Dharma has even turned, we have already laid out the Wheel of Food.
Crossing waters and piercing through clouds, you have not shied away from toil and hardship. As you stand at the parting of ways, I hope you will listen well to these few words.
After a long silence, he said: "When meeting a blue-eyed one on the road, do not boast; there is no need to recount the depths of Mount Baiyun. He then descended from his seat.
Thereupon, he invited the Head Seat to ascend the hall. Striking once with his staff, he said: "O Great Assembly, do you understand?

The spring season draws to a close; the weather is gradually warming. Flowers bloom high and low across the thousand peaks; mist shrouds the green trees near and far. The orioles sing and the valleys echo;
cranes and phoenixes soar in their graceful postures. The farmers rejoice in the bountiful harvests of Yao and Shun; the fishermen delight in..."
The Way of Ascending Peace: the moon rises at the edge of the clouds; the sun shines across the vast sky. The golden cock, holding a phoenix chick, returns to its nest;
the jade hare crosses the Milky Way, stirring the waves. Spiritual sprouts compete to emerge; withered trees welcome the spring. A single band of white clouds unfolds before the green mountains;
flowing waters traverse a thousand rivers, merging into one stream. Even when it reaches such a state, it is still a matter of "this side. It has fallen into the present.

"At that time, O worthy ones, what is the matter of 'that side'? After a long silence, he said: 'Where the snow is deep on the path through the ten-thousand-year pines, a range of peaks has the clouds rising even higher. He then descended from his seat."

When Master Yinyun arrived at the monastery, he ascended the hall and said: "In the Hall of No Shadow, who is the one who knows the music? Beside the ancient path, there are illusory men and wooden horses.
A thousand peaks lock in their emerald green; ten thousand trees hold the mist. Where white clouds arise, the gates of the pavilions open;
when azure mists roll away, the wondrous peak-tops are revealed. But tell me: how do you express the single phrase of meeting at the absolute summit?"
[He] said, "The Way. After a long silence, he said, "Not declining the distance of the mountain path, I have come specifically to enter the Pine Gate.
He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "The late spring has just ended and we enter early summer; everyone says today is the eighth day of the fourth month.
A stone sprout grows in the Lumbinī Garden; on Mount Wutai the wind whistles. The wooden rooster crows at the tile roof; the dog barks at Shide. Cold."
The mountains are as if in spring sleep. Old Wang of the eastern village burns paper money at night; its light flickers, making Mount Sumeru’s peaks tower ever higher.

[He] descends from his seat. On the occasion of the Imperial Birthday, he ascends the hall: Ten thousand *li* of Yao’s clouds, a thousand peaks of Shun’s rain. A rainbow’s radiance pierces before the Dipper and Ox constellations; its colors—
The vital energy (qi) forms an arch toward the wonders of the stars; the golden wheel rises like a fan, and the jade palace manifests auspicious omens.

The light and favor bring the springtime to the myriad nations, while Heaven enriches the longevity of the One Man. Therefore, when the teachings of the various sages are realized, they are efficacious;
within the rank of a human king, one is the most honored among human kings; within the rank of a Dharma King, one is the most honored among Dharma Kings. O virtuous ones!
"What is the Dharma of all the sages? After a long silence, he said: "With robes draped, he presides over the ten thousand nations; the constellations align with the three elders.
Small Assembly (Xiao Can). Master Yaoshan held a small assembly; when the congregation had gathered, the Master said: "I have a single phrase; I shall wait for a special [occasion]..."
When the cow gave birth to a calf, [Dongshan] immediately said to you, "At that time, a monk came forward and said, 'The cow has given birth to a special calf.
From then on, the Master did not speak further. Dongshan said, "Bring some fire! That monk then hid himself among the assembly.
Dongshan commented, "It was actually this monk who knew [the truth], yet he simply refused to prostrate. The Master said, "Great assembly, tell me: where exactly was it that this..."
The monk understands the underlying principle. If he can speak it, one may say he has cleared this monk’s grievance;
if he cannot speak it, he is instead deceived by Yaoshan. Tonight, this mountain monk, not begrudging his eyebrows, shall break it open for you all with a verse:
"How could a single phrase be bestowed by the Patriarchs and Buddhas? A special ox gives birth to a child in these present times. In the darkness, a single melody is faintly recognizable."
The lamp illuminates the fragmentary texts; they do not resemble poetry. [The Master] descends from his seat. Ascending the hall, he says:
"In solitary villages and humble alleys, do not hang up your bowls and alms-basins. At the profound barrier of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, pass straight through with your body horizontal.
Already, like Su Wu, you have touched the frontier walls; seeking a way back is difficult. When Xiang Yu faced the river, how could he escape his fated destiny? O virtuous practitioners of Zen!"
"Arriving here, to advance is to fall into the realm of celestial Māras; to retreat is to sink into the destiny of ghosts.

If one neither advances nor retreats, one remains right within the waters of death. How, O virtuous ones, can you attain stability? After a long silence, he said: "Let the three-foot snow fall as it will;
it cannot suppress the single inch of the spiritual pine. He stood for a long time and then said, "Take care."

The donor invited [the Master] to ascend the hall and said: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to present this matter. Yet, from the beginning, people have been unable to grasp it. Why is this?

If one discusses this matter, it is like a lute held in the palm; when the fingertips are skillfully employed, the seven strings are as taut as the wind, and the ten fingers pluck them like flowing water.
If there is even the slightest obstruction by a speck of dust, the sound will surely violate the fundamental tone."
"Shang" refers to the deliberate arrangement [of sounds]. Hearing necessarily differs from seeing and listening. Sometimes it loftily upholds the pure model;
there is not a single word where Buddhas and Patriarchs can find footing. Furthermore, having brought all commands to completion, throughout kalpas, both sages and ordinary beings have left no trace.
This is not to be dismissed as mere play; I shall briefly unfold a subtle sound, spreading the resonance that shakes the five heavens and the earth, singing the melody unheard by the Ten Sages.
It was as if mountains shook and oceans trembled, as flowers rained down and clouds flew. The hundred beasts were struck with alarm, and the gods and spirits were cowed with fear.

It spread throughout the ten directions, and both Hu and Han shared in the same wind; yet this was still merely falling within the gate of transformation—it was not yet the time of one's own fundamental portion.
"Virtuous ones, what is the time of one's fundamental nature? After a long silence, he said: "Since Boya has passed away, Ziqi has ceased playing the *Guangling* [lute].
To play the melodies of the Qin era in vain. He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Shishuang, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shishuang gnashed his teeth. The monk did not understand; he waited until after Shishuang had passed away before asking Jiufeng, "The former master gnashed his teeth—what was the underlying intent? Jiufeng said, "I would rather have my tongue cut off than violate the national taboo. He then asked Yungai, who said: [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "A monk once asked Shishuang, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shishuang gnashed his teeth. The monk did not understand and waited until Shishuang had passed away to ask Jiufeng, 'The former master gnashed his teeth; what was the meaning of that? Jiufeng replied, 'I would rather have my tongue cut off than violate the national taboo. He then asked Yungai, and Yungai said: [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "A monk once asked Shishuang, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shishuang gnashed his teeth. The monk did not understand and waited until Shishuang had passed away to ask Jiufeng, 'The former master gnashed his teeth; what was the meaning of that? Jiufeng replied, 'I would rather have my tongue cut off than violate the national taboo. He then asked Yungai, and Yungai said: [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "A monk once asked Shishuang, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shishuang gnashed his teeth. The monk did not understand and waited until Shishuang had passed away to ask Jiufeng, 'The former master gnashed his teeth; what was the meaning of that? "What grievance do I have with my former teacher? Friends, tell me: do these three venerable elders possess the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

"I, this mountain monk, shall disregard my very life to reveal this to you all. After a long silence, he said, "The weather is hot; take care of your eyebrows.

Later, when the Master was invited by a patron at Mount Simian to ascend the seat—this being the fourth time—he said, "Dharma assembly, just now..."
The various venerable elders may be said to have handed over the matter completely; what more could this mountain monk possibly say? Have you not seen the ancient saying:

To sing of the wondrous and discourse on the profound is like marking the boat a myriad miles away from its destination. Even if one were to realize it prior to the time of Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, it would still be the same as being lost.
A person on the road may even attain mastery beneath a single phrase; how is this different from the man who lost his pearl? Therefore, Master Dongshan said:
"Outside the night-bright curtain, the ancient mirror shines in vain; within the Hall of the Jewel King, the thousand lights cannot illuminate.
You must clarify the essential point among the heterodox; grasp it within the speech of the stone man. Gentlemen, what is this "stone man"?
[The Master] said: "If you can speak it, it may be said that beneath a thousand ages we share the same wind today. If you cannot speak it, I, this mountain monk, shall violate my own decree.
After a long silence, he said: "The ox and the dipper pass through the central palace; the great sun faces the vast ocean. Be careful!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The White Cloud Peak is distant; the green waters flow long. Colorful clouds enshroud the night moon as the stars rise high;

The straw dog barks at spring; the monkeys vie for their offspring. A stone ox crosses the ridge; a wooden horse turns its course.
Meeting at midnight—who can fully comprehend it? O virtuous ones, tell me: how do you speak that single phrase which does not fall into light or darkness?
After a long silence, he said: "Auspicious colors enshroud the misty peaks; white clouds disperse over the evening stream. He descended from his seat.

"How many people have passed over the ridge on the mountain path? After a long silence, he said, "Do not speak of how many there are beyond the river;

On the day of opening the furnace, he ascended the hall and said: "O Great Assembly! Within the flames of the red furnace, we together guard the cold ice;
amidst the sound of water and stones, we sit in silent seclusion. Frost welcomes the moonlight; pines lock in the blue smoke.

There is no dharma to transmit to Kāśyapa; his tracks remain on Mount Xiong’er. As I go forth, I tread upon the snow of the steps; spring departs, and how many autumns shall pass before I return?

The sun shines by day, the crying monkeys are pained; the clouds part to reveal the gurgling flow of water. At the temple beneath the woods on the western peak, an old man rests in leisure among ancient pines.
At the first watch of night, clouds rise from the rocks; the monkeys cry out as rain falls upon the western peak. For nine years at Shaoshi, the man cooked his vegetables in a potless cauldron.
Master Dongcun Wang disliked excessive talk; he took up his single sandal and returned home. He specifically did not grant permission.
Shaolin is an ancient monastery; how many times has it been visited? The mountain stream cuts diagonally through the eastern ridge; the rain ruins the stone gate, leaving it fallen.
A wooden man picks up his lamp at night; who else shall sweep the hermitage floor? The moon sets and the clear breeze grows cold; the mountain pines let the vines grow old.
The golden coffin reveals the two feet; more than two thousand years have passed. Sitting with face to the wall at Shaolin—this is neither samādhi nor dhyāna.
The stone man walks away treading through the snow; the wooden horse sleeps amidst the flames. What is the purpose of these three prostrations? One arm is transmitted from antiquity to the present.

The mountain stream is as clear as a mirror; flowers bloom upon the crags like woven patterns. Though there are thousands of variations in height and depth, all are sustained by the power of non-discrimination.
The eyes see nothing but absolute stillness; what the ears hear does not deviate from the mind. Faith and concentration are like adamant; the initial resolve perfects ten thousand virtues.

Clouds roll away and all peaks are revealed; the pine wind sounds like rain at the gate. This was once a place where the Dharma was transmitted; the trees are ancient and the resident birds have returned.

The moon over the mountain stream is clear and cold with snow; the cries of the monkeys grow fainter by the moment. I feel ashamed and humbled by these ancient matters; perhaps cutting off one’s arm is a rare occurrence to compare with this.
Following the ancients, I describe the twelve periods of the day:
at the hour of Chou (1–3 a.m.), when the cock crows, I wake up and find there is nothing to do. Unable to avoid it, I put on my robe and don my cloth skirt before the brazier of cold ashes.
The cold borders are guarded by cats;

at dawn, it is the hour of Yin. Never have I been as poor as this year. Since long ago, the path to those who understand me has been utterly lost. I gaze in vain against the sparse window, my brows furrowing again and again.

At dawn in the hour of the Rabbit, cease your diligent practice and cease your calculating. Even if you manage to deceive those to the west, you will still be bitten by the dog at the fence of the eastern village.
At the time of eating, you look up and do not recognize who your kin are; you force a smile to address others, yet it is utterly insincere.
Huì again gave rise to anger.
By the hour of wǔ (9–11 a.m.), when the deserted dwelling was empty, a weary, blue-skinned, and lame boy suddenly arrived.
He said, "The Way has made me your disciple."

At noon in the land south of the sun, the rice bowl arrives and shatters the household furniture. Ceasing worldly ways to leave home and embrace a life of ease, one devours the boundless moss of hunger and toil.

At the hour of *ri-dik* (the fifth watch, approximately 3:00–4:59 PM): I urge you to cease dwelling in the realm of fame and profit; even the Buddha-way, my own native land, I am too lazy to tread upon.

Let others revile me as being devoid of gratitude and righteousness. At the hour of *pu-shi* (the sixth watch, approximately 5:00–6:59 PM): Even if one were to attain profound awakening, it would not be more intimate than this: it is better to simply accept things as they are, moment by moment. May this year come to an end [in this way].
The spring returns once again.
When the sun enters the hour of You (5–7 p.m.), the cool hare departs; there is no need to guard it further. The sun rises over the western mountains while the northern mountains grow bright.
One cannot believe that Mount Sumeru runs through the void.
The hour of Xu (7–9 p.m.): Cease speaking of the foreign monk sitting at Shaoshi; in the end, when hungry, one is hungry for oneself.
Who would believe these idle words and noisy chatter?
The hour of Hai (9–11 p.m.): Mice come calling in swarms. Reflecting that there is nothing left to gnaw upon, give them a piece of wood.
The pillow would not even accept it.

At midnight, during the hour of Zi, he dreamed that he obtained money and died of joy; upon waking, he searched for it, but not a single coin was there. Who would have known that such a state of delusion could reach this point?

The Fisherman (Two Poems) I drift on a solitary boat where not an inch of land remains. What cause for worry that royal service shall call upon my door? Mountains reflect in the azure waves, soaking the ancient melodies.
In pure clouds and mist, who could ask further of Buddha or the Patriarchs?
At dawn, the wind subsides and the misty waves settle. Gently rowing my small boat, I indulge in this leisurely delight. Before my eyes, the autumn river is as clear as a mirror;
the bright moon hangs high, further enhanced by the reflection of reeds on both banks.
A Brief Letter on News from the Eastern House to Guizong’s Chief Seat, An: The peak of Shaoshi is high; the stars turn at its corner. Last night, the phoenix carried off the vermilion cassia;
this morning, the stone tiger roars into the vast void. The sun adds to the red flames while the jade branches grow cold; the moon faces the golden wheel and the purple [clouds].
The breath is relaxed. Amidst my leisure, I venture to set forth the matters of dwelling in the mountains: the fragrant *utpala* flower in the imperial garden;
the snow-capped peaks of Shao-lin where the ancient terrace is bare;
no more talk of the Westward Coming, lest it deceive you. To seek the Way only serves to increase one's emotional entanglements.
Noisy clamor! If one is willing to come, after the letter, both sage and ordinary are empty. Fragrance blooms upon withered wood as spring lengthens; red flames and blue lotuses unfold in summer.
I venture to rely on these clumsy verses to report from afar: the lush greenery stretches on, with cypress trees and the rising moon.

When Elder Ping passed away on the road, Dao Shang still frowned; when words meet in silent resonance, how could the vital function be lost? One must reach the place where the sick man rebukes the layman;
then naturally, one wears the robe of the Patriarch without attachment. At midnight in Xiao and Xiang, the golden crow dawns; at the break of day by the Luo River, the jade rabbit shines.
The phoenix returns. One who knows the sound now entrusts it to beneath the forest. The withered tree welcomes the majestic wind, its fruit ripening and swelling.
In leisurely discourse, I send this to you;

though human emotions have various conditions that stir them, when the mind is empty, all affairs come to rest. Not only are the ordinary and the sage severed from conceptualization, but upon encountering things, one naturally has no seeking.
Non-seeking is in harmony with the Way; how could the Way ever conflict with non-seeking? Clouds disperse across the azure sky as the full moon shines afar;
the green mountains rise like mounds, their verdant hues growing upon one's robes.
I pay homage at the stupa of the Third Patriarch, Master Jianzhi:

The mountain peak’s approach is vast and distant; The sacred stupa locks the clouds in its height. With staff and almsbowl, the spring flows with the moon; The three portions of śarīra are concealed within.
I pay homage at the stupa of the Fourth Patriarch, Chan Master Dayi:
A single stupa beneath the twin peaks, his entire body before the myriad phenomena. How many times have the pines aged in their coldness? The full moon never departs from the sky.

The Chan Master of Jingzhai personally founded this site; the Holy Sovereign, the King of Physicians, proclaimed its excellence. Now that the Ox-Head man is gone, the wind and smoke reach the eastern ridges.
I pay homage at the stupa of the Fifth Patriarch, Chan Master Daman.

Its tower rises beyond a thousand peaks, a solitary seat towering with dignity. The Dharma was transmitted as a seal from the Fourth Patriarch; the robe was entrusted to the one who pounded rice in Lingnan.

Master Songzhu planted these himself; their further growth is a sacred mystery beyond fathoming. In the late night, the moon reflects upon the lotus pond; the bell chimes as the wind stirs the mountains and valleys.

At Tiantong’s Compassionate Salvation Pagoda, the white clouds cannot hold it back—by what could the green ridges contain them? Moonlight enshrouds the cold pagoda; the sound of pines fills the midnight autumn.

The Goose Pagoda of Dharma Master Huiyuan of Mount Lu has endured for over eight hundred years. It has weathered many storms and witnessed countless springs. Though the carts once used at Tiger Creek have long since vanished and the village folk are scattered, the pine steps remain as they were, casting their eternal shade of green.
The Pagoda of Chan Master Yunju Hongjue:
Continuing the lineage of Yaoshan, Yuyan, and Dongshan, the peaks of Ou join the lush greenery, casting shadows over the mundane world. Though a path leads to the azure heavens, who comes and goes?
Only the stone man traverses the bird-path with ease. The pagoda locks within the emerald forest as a thousand ridges stretch afar; the broken stele remains amidst the ten-thousand moons.
In the mountain stream, as we now pay homage once more to the legacy of the lineage, let us raise our voices in song to continue the tradition of the Hu family.
The stupa of Chan Master Chaya, the fourth generation of Tong’an, cannot be sought beyond the reaches of time;
yet one beholds the true form within the empty hall, where the vermilion phoenix comes to perch upon the green peaks.
Afterwards, the golden dragon departed; the stream flows by and the jade steps are new. The pagoda seals the colors of dawn, while auspicious winds blow afar.
Creepers cling to the incense altar, a neighbor to the night moon. How shall one inquire of the news from the nine peaks? Seek it within the body beyond heaven and earth.
The Wayfarer of the Fields at Shuangxi Temple, Daozhen:

His Way exists across the ages; where have the people of past and present gone? The stream divides its headwaters and comes bearing the moon. By the crags stand ancient pines, by the graves grow bamboos;
their pure resonance stirs from time to time upon the steps of the Patriarchs’ Hall.
True Portrait Eulogy for Chan Master Huangbo Duanji:

Mount Baizhang is majestic; the precipice of Duanji is steep. When the moon fills the vast ocean, his eyes grow dim and his ears deaf. He sticks out his tongue and shrinks his neck, and Linji submits to him.
A single snowflake flies within a cauldron of boiling broth; amidst the kalpa-fire that consumes the heart, the red jade remains moist.
True Portrait Eulogy for Master Touzi Jue Kai:
Tranquil dwelling amidst cold pines; the ancestral peak bathed in a chill moonlight. Upon close inspection of his compassionate countenance, he is majestic yet not fierce.
Before the fifth watch, when the stars and constellations shift, A snow-dappled ox plows through the shadows of the moon.
Eulogy for the Portrait of Master Touzi Yuan:
Before Mount Jiuli, he cannot be found; The moon fills the Chu River west of Baofeng Peak. At night’s depth, clouds embrace the path of Longmian;
For twelve years, the sound of pines has harmonized with the ten thousand籁 (resonances).
Eulogy for Chan Master Touzi Zhengwu:
Clouds gather over a thousand peaks; the moon flows through the four seas. The bones are hidden in two lands; the Way is without change or alteration.
Tranquil dwelling amidst layered mists and deep trees, The crimson sun divides its rosy hues in the dead of night.
Eulogy for Chan Master Zhiguang of Zhidu Mountain in Luzhou: His Way connects to Panshan;
his path leads directly across. Silently accepting the divine covenant, what need has he to heed ghosts or tigers? The ten-thousand-year pine grows old upon the ancient cliff’s greenness;
A single moon flows through the void, and the mountain peaks are revealed.
True Portrait Eulogy for Chan Master Dongshan Wuben:

The waters of Dong Creek flow upstream; the path to Yunyan connects here. Crossing ridges and fording streams, he advances and retreats according to his own course. When the moon comes, the phoenix rests beneath the trees;
as the wind rises high over the emerald peaks, misty trees layer upon one another.
True Eulogy for Master Liangshan:

The dragon gives birth to dragon cubs; the phoenix gives birth to phoenix chicks. The pines atop ten thousand ridges are lofty; when the spring breeze moves them, A single robe gathers the clouds at Yangguang City;
Mount Tong’an reveals the moon over Ou Peak.
Eulogy for the Portrait of Chan Master Dayang An:
The ancient sail is not raised; the shadowless tree grows. Its leaves cover the front cliff; its fragrance perfumes the ridge behind.
At midnight, the golden cock arrives with its chick; At daybreak, the colorful phoenix departs with the clouds.
True Inscription for Chan Master Yuanjian of Fushan in Shuzhou:
The jade tree has no place for the phoenix to perch; The moon over the Golden River has not yet risen. A wooden man comes to beg for fire— At midnight, the great spring sun shines forth.
A Zen practitioner painted a portrait of his teacher and requested a eulogy.

Upon suddenly examining the transmitted ritual protocols, I find there is nothing at all with which to compare it; it is not that of a monk, nor can one hope for even a grain or a pint of its likeness. White clouds embrace the rocky crags through the night;
the moon rises over a thousand peaks as the morning mist clears from the green ridges.
Yang Cigong’s Praise of the Master’s Portrait:
A single sandal, two pieces of leather. Where the golden oriole cries, the wooden cock flies. At midnight, the oil-seller bursts into laughter.
A white-haired man gives birth to a black-haired child.

Master Si questioned the Great Master Huineng, saying, "What should one attend to so as not to fall into stages?
The Master replied, "What have you been doing? Si said, "I do not even engage in the Noble Truths. The Master asked, "In what stage do you then fall?"
Ji said, "If even the Noble Truths are not to be practiced, what 'stages' could there possibly be? The Patriarch said, "So it is, so it is.
You must maintain this well; I shall have a verse for you: 'The ground of the mind contains all seeds,' and so forth."
The crown of the head is invisible as clouds gather in haste; the numinous branch beyond the kalpas bears no spring.
Not sitting in the palace of the Sovereign of Emptiness, how could one be willing to till the fields toward the solar wheel?
Shitou was brought before Master Si. Si asked, "Where have you come from? Shitou replied, "From Caoxi.
Si then held up his whisk and said, "Is there such a thing as this at Caoxi? Shitou said, "Not only at Caoxi; even in the Western Heavens there is none.
Si said, "Have you perhaps been to the Western Heavens? Shitou replied, "If I had gone..."
When [Zhaozhou] said, "It exists," Yunmen replied, "Not yet; say it again. Zhaozhou said, "Do not rely entirely on me; you, Master, must also speak half of it.
Yunmen said, "I do not refuse to speak to you, but I fear that later there will be no one to take it up."
White clouds conceal the jade phoenix; the red sun shines without distance. Where the stars cluster in dimness, the Impartial One presides over the nine heavens.
When Yaoshan and Yunyan were traveling through the mountains, a sword sounded at Yaoshan’s waist. Yunyan asked, "What object is making that sound?"
The Mountain draws his blade and makes a gesture of cutting across his own throat;
the Great Peng passes the Celestial Lake without a companion. The Lion carries its cub, following it to the end; Kunlun, having committed an offense, returns to his path.
A single aperture swallows the clouds as the ten thousand phenomena race forth.
The Master raised an instance where a monk asked Dao Wu, "What is the Master’s profoundest place?
Dao Wu descended from his meditation seat, performed a woman’s bow, and said, "Thank you for coming from afar; there is nothing else with which to entertain you."

The black dragon lies coiled in the sea, auspicious clouds rise high; from every direction they return to the source, as ten thousand streams flow toward the morning court. A wooden man comes to inquire of the affairs of the Western Palace;
he is granted in return a single peach from the Eastern Garden.
When Yunyan first visited Yaoshan, Yaoshan asked, "Where have you come from? Yunyan replied, "I have come from Baizhang.
Yaoshan asked, "What words or phrases did he speak? Yunyan said, "At times he would say that a single phrase contains all flavors. Yaoshan then said:
"Salty" is the taste of saltiness; "bland" is the taste of blandness. That which is neither salty nor bland is the constant taste.
"What is the phrase for possessing all hundred flavors? Yanguan had no reply. Guishan said, "What can you do about birth and death right before your eyes?
Yanguan said, "There is no birth and death right before my eyes. Guishan said, "Having spent twenty years at Baizhang, you have not even removed your worldly airs. Furthermore—
The questioner asked, "Brother Hai, what further Dharma did you speak? Yan said, "Sometimes I say: 'Beyond the three phrases, let go; beyond the six phrases, realize.
Shan said, 'Even from three thousand miles away, I am glad there is no connection [with that]. Shan asked again, 'What further Dharma did you speak?
Yan said, 'Sometimes, after the assembly has finished descending from the hall following the lecture, I call out to them once more.'"
The assembly turned their heads in unison, and he asked, "What is this? Shanshan said, "Why did you not speak like this earlier?
At these words, Yanyuan attained realization.

Having traversed the paths of a thousand peaks, the road grows ever higher; only when one is willing to return does one remember the old cloud-cloaked chamber. One greedily seeks the ancient melody of the Xianyu flute.
Verse: The tune extends through the *cuo-hu* rhyme family.
I cite Jia Shan’s study under Chuan Zi:
Paddling a boat across the perils for thirty springs, A "living dead man" at the tip of the pole where the blow lands. The cassia branches of Jia Ling have divided for a thousand ages.
The rhyme: The green of the mountains and rivers is renewed in ten thousand ways.
Yun-lang [recites]: When Yaoshan asked the novice Gao, "I have heard that Chang'an is very noisy," Gao replied, "In my country, all is peaceful.
Yaoshan said with delight, "Did you obtain this from reading the scriptures, or did you obtain it from washing your bowls? Gao replied, "Neither from reading the scriptures..."
"Obtained through reading the sutras, yet not obtained by requesting a bath. Shanshan said, "There are many who do not read sutras and do not request a bath;
why do they not obtain it? Mili said, "I do not say that they cannot obtain it; it is simply that they are unwilling to take responsibility for it."
Rising and falling are like clouds passing by; he has no land and is free from all dust.
Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru grows a rootless grass that, untouched by the spring breeze, blooms of its own accord.
A monk asked Shishuang, "What is the Master’s profound depth? Shishuang replied: "No need for a lock—the two ends sway;
at the third watch the moon sets and the two mountains shine bright. On the ancient road the journey is long and moss grows thick; when the golden lock sways, there are no hands."
[This is] an offense. The rabbit of the moon in the heart’s blue waves constantly moves.
A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Dongshan said, "Wait until the waters of the Dong River flow backward, and I will tell you."
In the ancient source there is no water; how could the moon arise? A single stream flows westward, dividing along the banks. Cease inquiring about the dream of Xiong’er at Mount Xi;
desist from speaking of the spring at Shaolin in the snowy courtyard.
A monk asked Jia Shan, "What is the Buddha? Shan replied, "In this place, there is neither guest nor host.
The monk asked, "With whom do you usually converse? Shan said, "Mañjuśrī has already gone to fetch water; Samantabhadra has not yet returned with the flowers."

Of those who know the words of the Master as he spoke them, how many are there? From antiquity to the present, none have been his peer, and none can equal him. A jade horse gallops through the snow, returning at the dead of night;
a goral hangs from its horns as the moon sinks in the west.

Yungai asked Shishuang, "I do not ask about the time when ten thousand doors are all open; but what is it like when ten thousand doors are all closed? Shishuang replied, "What is the matter within the hall?

Yungai had no answer. After half a year, he finally spoke these words: [He remained silent. (Note: The source text ends with "葢無對" (Yungai had no answer) and mentions that after six months he finally spoke; the specific words he spoke are not provided in the fragment.)
"No one can grasp him," Zhaozhou said. Shuangfeng remarked, "If you speak of it, you have spoken it too much; even so, you have only captured eighty percent.
Zhaozhou asked, "What about you, Master? Shuangfeng replied, "No one can recognize him."
In the ancient hall, the cliffs open and the moon locks the pines; Frost gathers and snow falls, their resonance inexhaustible. Before the stars, one lies in a chamber amidst a thousand peaks;
Even Buddhas and Patriarchs have no means to recognize him.
A monk asked Master Jiufeng Qian, "Why was it that Sengyao could not capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong with a single stroke of his brush?
The Master said, "Sengyao actually received the seal of approval from Zhigong. The monk asked, "I do not understand; what kind of person did Sengyao take as his witness?
Jiufeng said, "The tortoise bows its head to the pillar of Mount Sumeru."
Jing Mountain’s jade was sought by the man of Bian; the supreme treasure is flawless, utterly transcending causes and conditions. An iron ox with its calf treads the vast ocean;
a stone tortoise that strikes the moon grows long feathers and scales.
A monk asked Shao Shan, "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase? Shan said, "There is. The monk asked, "What phrase is it?
Shan said, "A single mass of solitary clouds does not reveal its ugliness."
White clouds do not reach the summit of the central peak; The scenery of misty vines fills the eyes, truly extraordinary. A single phrase contains the melody of a thousand ages;
Amidst ten thousand layers of azure green, the moon first appears.
A monk asked Liangshan, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Shan said, "Do not speak recklessly. The imperial decree is strict;
those who attempt to contrive it stand in peril. A mere hair’s breadth of movement brings the iron wheel; as soon as a thought sprouts in the mind, the mouth responds three thousand *li* away.
Teeth bared and words spoken—who can bear such bitter resentment?"
A monk asked Longya about the fundamental meaning of the Patriarchs:
"Who hears the conversation of the stone tortoise? The earless skull listens deeply at night;
only when dawn breaks does it hide in the shadowless tree, which the great sun may shine upon yet cannot find."
Lingyun saw the peach blossoms and attained enlightenment:

Before the mountain, the peach blooms with the spring of his old garden; The flowers open on red branches as he reflects upon this body. To provide proof, he thanks the guest for exerting effort beside him;
Though a smile is displayed, a sense of resentment arises. Smoke locks the green willows as the oriole’s song lingers slow; Rain invades the stone pillar as he leans against it.
The void is neighbor to the void. The golden crow has flown away with no news; the wooden horse’s neighing passes through Han and Qin.
Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Huizhong: "What do you require after a hundred years?"

The ancient pagoda surged with holiness, leaving the deluded at a loss; clouds enshrouded it, and the dragons and phoenixes vanished. The fragrant breeze sank into the dead of night, and within the jeweled hall there was no one to recognize it.
Layman Pang asked Master Ma: "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion? The Master said:
"Wait until you can suck up all the waters of the West River in a single gulp, and then I shall tell you."
"Parents have been separated for a long time; when you meet them, you must serve them with all your strength. At midnight, a wooden man spoke: "Do not let outsiders know this.
A monk asked Changsha, "Does the person who is originally so become a Buddha? Changsha said, "Tell me, does the Emperor of the Great Tang cut thatch grass?"
Moss-covered halls layer upon layer, where purple vapors deepen; the stars divide their positions, setting the Great Unity (Qian Kun) right. The Golden Wheel does not govern the realm of Jambudvīpa;
how could it compare to the precious seals of the feudal lords?
Daowu and Yunyan went to Nanquan. Nanquan asked, "What is the name of the *ācārya*? Daowu replied, "Zongzhi.
Nanquan said, "At the place where wisdom does not reach, how can there be a 'principle' (*zong*)? Daowu said, "One must strictly avoid speaking of it.
Nanquan said, "Indeed; if you speak of it, horns will grow. On another day, while Daowu and Yunyan were mending clothes with needles in the rear quarters, Nanquan [entered].
The Master asked again. The Dharma Master Zhi said, "Regarding that which the Way-intelligence does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it.
If one speaks of it, then 'horns' will grow. How, then, should one practice? Thereupon, I withdrew my body and entered the Sangha hall.
Ancient skulls beneath the Vajra-limit have been trodden by many, their blood splashing into the void. Let you freely cup the bright moon in your hands;
how could the cold pines abandon their shroud of white clouds?
Whenever a monk approached, Zhaozhou would immediately ask, "Have you been here before? If the monk said, "I have not," Zhaozhou would say, "Go drink tea.
