As the blue smoke darkened, it was replaced by green-veined moss.
The Public Case of the Great Following-Along Covering Turtle:
When one house has business, a hundred houses are busy. When spring warmth returns, the grass grows of its own accord. The moon on the eastern ridge divides the waters of the western ravine;
though the wine is exhausted, they still wait for the Double Ninth Festival.
At Nanquan, the two halls disputed over a cat;
when facing danger, one must know how to push others aside. Seeking talent first reveals one's own needle and chisel; those who fish all speak of the hidden currents.
But when the wind actually arrives, the waves obscure the path. Though the weary Zhaozhou was a skilled hand, he went to the meal after the bell had rung.
"Coming late. One must know that the Great Elephant guards the road to Jiazhou; the Iron Ox firmly blocks the pass of Shaanxi.
A monk asked Yunju Hongjue, "Ultimately, what is the way for a monastic? Yunju replied, "The mountains of Yunju are beautiful."
Lofty and towering, ten thousand fathoms wide; no path exists on its four sides for passage. Since ancient times, the light of the two wheels has never reached here;
at night’s depth, the old king enters the western peak.
One day, while passing by, Danxia stayed overnight at a monastery;
as the cold was intense, he burned a wooden Buddha. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Not knowing how to be a guest, you trouble the host.
Ancient crags are sealed by moss and cold invades the door; those who fly are struck with peril, and those who run are lost. Deep in the night, the cold fire burns upon the marshy isles."
Fire! At dawn, the fisherman was busy and grew suspicious of himself.
He brought up his visit to Jia Shan; Shan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix's nest is not of its kind. Get out! (and so forth).
A companionless stone man enters the mountains at night; snow enshrouds his crimson peak as his green robes shiver in the cold.
With a shout, he cleaves the summit of the three peaks at the dawn of the kalpa, holding aloft the golden robe to gaze upon the sun.
A monk asked Shushan, “What is the Buddha? He replied, “Why do you not ask this old fellow Shushan?
Only by raising children does one know the compassion of the parent above. The words of a relative have no flavor; outsiders harbor doubts.
If you wish to exhaust the deepest reaches of the Canglang River, listen to the fisherman’s song and do not be deluded.”
A monk asked Master Chongyun, "What is it to return to the root and attain the essential meaning? Chongyun said: "Long ago I forgot and did not remember the arising of dust;
the house is broken and the people are gone—where can one rely? Without mind and without sequence, I speak of seeking a home; for ten years I have forgotten the way I came."
On the road, though I recall it for a brief moment, I know nothing at all.
A monk asked Jia Shan, "What is the realm of Jia Shan? Jia Shan said, "The monkey carries its young back behind the green peaks;
the bird holds flowers in its beak as they fall before the azure cliffs."

The moon is bright, the pines are green, and the crane’s dream is long; Azure clouds and crimson cassias hang like a wild sheep. High crags and towering walls are covered in snow from a thousand peaks;
Stone sprouts grow branches amidst the midnight frost.
A monk asked Caoshan, "What was it like before the Buddha appeared in the world? and so forth.

The moon hides behind the green mountains as auspicious vapors rise high; The variegated phoenix dwells in the wutong trees, gazing into the boundless void. Without cause, a stone horse passes through the depths of the pool;
Startling the clay dragon, who overturns the ocean tides.
A monk asked Yunju, "If there is no place at all to learn, how does one establish oneself? Yunju said, "There is no place to establish oneself.
The monk said, "Then what need is there for the work of Buddha? Yunju said, "It is not the same as Xinghua's."

Moss-covered halls gather the mist as purple vapors swirl; the courtiers bow before the imperial dais, withdrawing in the age of Yao. The phoenix perches and does not stay among the guests of Peach Blossom Spring;
how could it ever gaze upon the golden light of the Han heavens?
A monk asked Fengxue, "When there is no melody or rhythm in an ancient tune, how can one harmonize it?
Fengxue replied, "The wooden cock crows at midnight; the straw dog barks at daybreak."
Moonlight on ancient crags locks the heavy clouds; Withered trees welcome the fragrance, bearing spring at dawn. Last night the stars and river turned toward the Southern Dipper;
The golden sun followed the phoenix across the celestial wheel.
A monk asked Touzi, "What is it like when the kalpa-fire blazes forth? He replied, "It is chillingly majestic.
"Heaven and earth serve as the furnace, and all things are scorched; The stone man rides the waves across the clouds and mists. Wind arises in the dead of night, the frosty majesty grows heavy;
The moon sets in icy cold, pressing the hair at one's temples until it withers."
Mihu asked Yangshan, "In these times, do people still need to attain awakening? Yangshan replied, "Awakening is not non-existent;
however, it inevitably falls into the second rank. Mihu deeply approved of this.
I asked a person at the peak of the green crags; he pointed to the end of the mountains, yet had not settled there himself.
Though he may thus avoid the decree of the Double Ninth Festival, how can this compare to the numinous sprout that never offends the spring?
Jingqing asked Xuefeng, "An ancient said... Xuefeng then lay down on his back. After a long while, he rose and asked, "What did you ask?
Jingqing asked again. Xuefeng said, "A man who lives in vain and dies in waves."

Ordinarily, one longs for guests and regrets their absence; yet when they arrive, one is too weary to engage in conversation. Lying empty-handed, one realizes too late that sleep was not properly earned;
all toil has been in vain as the red flames fall into cold ashes.
One day Yunmen asked Mingjiao, "How many sesame cakes did you eat today? Mingjiao said, "Five.
Yunmen said, "How many did the pillar eat? Mingjiao said, "Please ask the Master to come to the tea hall for some tea."

Casually hanging down, he asks about the origins; not failing his lifelong commitment, he responds with a resolute "Tut! One must exert one's full strength for others until reaching the ultimate depth;
only then will one know that the taste of tea can dispel human sorrow.
A monk asked Yunju, "What is it like when the six gates are not clear? Yunju said, "It does not involve conditions.
The monk asked, "What about the matter that transcends this? Yunju said, "The cautious do not guard."
When spring arrives, the stone man gazes at the distant mountains; The oriole sings among flowering trees by the tranquil blue waves.
One must know that the auspicious rock-pines beyond the clouds Welcome the breeze for a thousand ages, enduring the cold of the seasons.
When Fengxue first arrived at Huanglong, Huanglong asked, "The stone horn pierces the path through the clouds; what is the meaning of the hanging cord?
Fengxue said, "Red clouds enshroud the jade image; the peaks embrace the valleys and plains. Huanglong said, "If that is so, then you have come along with me.
Fengxue said, "Master, lower your voice."
A priceless, bright pearl hangs in the darkness; at night, one attempts to pierce a wooden man.
Who would have known that it was seen by the earthen ox, who swallowed it whole into the depths of crimson clouds and azure waves?
When Master Xuefeng saw Elder Nanji off as he departed, he performed a woman’s bow. Nanji folded his hands and said, "Yes, yes.
Xuefeng struck his forehead with his hand and then returned.

Seeing off guests, I provide according to my family’s means, whether abundant or frugal; I bid them farewell with all sincerity so as to avoid giving rise to suspicion. Yet, having received your profound kindness, you have bestowed further gifts upon me;
with hands clasped in reverence, I take my leave from afar and return at twilight.
When Master Fu was visiting King Liang, he did not rise. An official asked him, "Why does the Great Being not rise when seeing the King?
The Master replied, "If the ground of Dharma were to move, all things would be unsettled."
The Master held up the staff and said: "To stabilize the state and quell disorder truly relies upon capable ministers; to establish the Dharma and clarify the school must depend on a master.
If the application of the opportunity is not subtle, one's transgressions will fill the heavens; if the power and function are incomplete, the transformative wind will be diminished by half.

If one follows the principle of 'lowering the high to reach the low,' it is like withered wood blooming at the Double Ninth festival; if one exhausts the command to sit with legs crossed, then the sorrow is shared across ten thousand li."
The Magistrate of Liang-land causes the State of Wei to grieve; crossing the river and plunging into the water, he follows the current unseen.
Although he dwells upon not even an inch of earth without moving, alas, the twin-sal trees are already half-autumn.
A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the point of intimacy for a student? Shoushan said, "The five nines end, and once again we meet spring.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? Shoushan said, "Winter has passed; Cold Food Festival is one hundred and five days away."
At twilight, dark clouds deepen the wilds and fields; after the arrival of the Double Ninth, fresh blossoms are gathered.
Were it not for the vanishing of the last ice on the western peaks, how could spring reach this stretch of the eastern mountains?
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? Yunmen said, "Steamed buns.
The discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs is questioned by a master; when weary, one should drink Jianxi tea. As the Double Ninth Festival approaches, the golden jar is opened;
deep-water fish swim, moving the sand in silence.
A monk asked Xuansha, "What is the matter directly transmitted by the Master? Xuansha said, "I am the son of the Xia family.
He personally extended the definitive truth to you; do not compare it to the transmission from Liusha or Shaoshi. Last night, the wild geese returned to the Twin Peaks.
Later, while Xie Jia was standing before Yueming, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, "The teeth on a wooden board grow hair."

Nine years at Shaoshi, one remains empty and adrift; how can this compare to the transmission of that single phrase right before one? Even if the teeth of a wooden board grow hair, it is still a matter worth attending to;
the stone man tramples the boat of the Xie family to pieces.
A monk asked Master Yong of Mount Yangshan, "What is the jewel of the Dharmakāya? He replied, "The hundred-tongued bird has not yet ceased its chatter on the branch;
how would the phoenix deign to roost with it?"

Pines grow by the crags and cranes rest securely; the phoenix emerges from the Vermilion Mountains accompanied by a flock of pheasants. Yet even facing the wall, one still falls short regarding matters beyond the hut;
why does Vimalakīrti trouble himself with such excessive discourse?
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Yunmen replied, "Looking at the mountains in broad daylight.
Tantan once asked Master An, "How does this compare to the single phrase transmitted by Shaoyang? 'The immortal’s palm on Mount Hua is revealed in the daylight;
at night, the monkey cries as the moon hangs before the window.'"
Citing the public case of Jia Shan while serving as the head cook at Mount Gui:
When meeting, one asks about the assembly of monks; do not compare it to the offering of fragrant meals in a hermitage garden. Purple qi follows the vermilion phoenix through the night;
The golden dragon coils around the branch of the moon at dawn.

A monk asked Baling, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? He replied, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water.
Regarding the source of the question on the meaning of the Patriarchs, he immediately repays him with that which is priceless: the fishing line descends as the night grows still.
Fishing: At dawn, one knows how to gather the golden crow along with the moon.
A monk asked Touzi, "How far apart are the ordinary and the sage? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there.

The waters flow from Kunlun, waves rolling on in succession; Heaven is high, earth is vast, and the forested peaks are exquisite. With a slight descent from the meditation seat, the clouds and mountains appear.
Severed. No trace of ordinary or sage; sea and mountains are cold.
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the Way? Zhaozhou said, "The one outside the wall.
To know the Way, one must rely on that venerable old man; his direct words and pointing are all in haste. The mountain pass road is long; one must traverse it again.
"Go! You may traverse the long road along the single path as you please.
Master Yong of Yangshan addressed the assembly, saying: "A single word exhausts the entirety of mountains and rivers. A monk then asked: "What is this one word?
Yangshan stuck his fire tongs into the side of the brazier and then withdrew them back to their original place.

A single phrase proclaims the differentiation of the myriad phenomena; who would be willing to close the heavy gates like those at Makula? Amidst the shadows of the setting sun, the wind and waves surge violently;
one does not realize the boat has drifted to the dusk of the ancient ferry.
A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the path to bodhi? Shoushan said, "Five li from here to Xiangyang.
The monk asked, "How about the matter that transcends this? Shoushan said, "Coming and going is no easy matter."
Asking the way at a crossroads, I prepare to advance on my journey; green willows and the song of orioles escort the traveler.
The signpost points out five li toward you—do not say that it did not indicate the path in years past.
A monk asked Yantou, "How is it when the ancient sail has not yet been hoisted? Yantou said, "The donkey in the back garden is eating grass.
The Master commented: "Hanshan’s sleep was deep; Shide took a long time to rouse him."

Clouds darken the western crags while the eastern ridges shine bright; from the southern marshes, the sound of a flute rises. The light of heaven is heavy with sleep as the robes are moistened by the dew;
the oriole warbles on high branches where willows bear the spring.
A monk asked Fengxue: "Deer and antelope form a herd; how can one shoot the leader among them? Fengxue said:
"The fishing boat has reached the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers; with breath choked and silence profound, one asks the white gulls."

The Forbidden Palace is surrounded by heavy enclosures; sight and hearing are perilous. I contemplate sideways and stand apart as the crimson cords hang down. In the land of Han, clouds are severed and the marsh islands stretch afar.
At twilight on the ridges, gibbons cry out as the solitary moon follows.
A monk asked Touzi, "Among the three bodies, which body preaches the Dharma? Touzi snapped his fingers. Regarding the origin of this question on the three bodies preaching the Dharma:
A light snap of the fingers gathers the seas and mountains; The golden-locked stupa opens to reveal the image of the red sun;
At night’s deep, people laugh upon the crest of the green peak.
A monk asked Master Yong of Yangshan, "What is the essential meaning of Caoxi? He replied: "A single lock enters the cold void.
Layered clouds reach high, piercing the cold void; The stupa is locked in deep clouds, its momentum inexhaustible. For a thousand ages, the sound of pines comes with its own melody;
For ten thousand years, the mountain stream flows away without a trace.
A monk asked Master Yunfeng Xian of Fuzhou, "What is one who stands above all Buddhas?
Yunfeng said, "White clouds cover the green mountains. The monk asked, "Is this not the very point where you benefit people?
Yunfeng said, "In the green pond, the lotuses grow in vain."
Layer upon layer of snow peaks, deep and locked in emerald mist; A wind rises from the cold ravines, binding thick clouds together. Last night, the vermilion phoenix soared toward the Milky Way;
At dawn, the woodsmen listen as they pursue the flocks of wild geese.
A monk asked Master Zhi of Guangjiao Monastery in Qizhou, "What is this thing? I, your student, do not understand.
Zhi said, "Born in Jizhou;
hemmed in by the heavy encampments of the imperial tent, the moss and lichen grow deep. The golden bell does not move, and there is no one to attend it. Who carries the staff to come and meet me?"
Question: It is said in response that "the wheat fields in the Eastern Garden are green.
A monk asked Fengxue, "What is the point of intimacy for a student? Fengxue said, "On the southern side of Mount Sumeru they beat the drums together;
on Mount Helan they spread out their leather robes to dry."
With kindness, he once extended a question to the old man: "Singing songs of the Eastern Mountain and chanting verses of the Northern Mountain—only a traveler from Jiang and Wu can master the tides;
for these words of parting, let them return to a man of Han."
A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the place where a student applies their mind? He replied, "I find it strange that your question is so late.

Before a word is spoken, it is difficult to clarify the states of delusion and awakening; only when one speaks can the person of sincere heart be revealed. People merely covet making progress to seek out clear jade;
how can they believe that the numinous sprout does not depend on spring?
A monk asked Shoushan, "All Buddhas emerge from this sutra. What is this sutra?
Shoushan said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. The monk asked, "How does one uphold it? Shoushan said, "Without defilement."
Water flows from Mount Kunlun and gives rise to clouds; the fisherman and the woodcutter are ignorant of their origins.
They know only the vastness of the surging waves and the rocky peaks, refusing to cast their lines or abandon the sound of their axes.
A monk asked the Venerable Huishou of Mount Zhaohe in Yingzhou, "What is the Buddha? He replied: "Looking from level ground toward a high ridge;
having traversed the mountains and rivers with much effort, one finally meets someone to speak of our past shared experiences. Spring has arrived at the southern wall of Lake Dongting."
The banks; birds cry out on the western ridge as the moon rises over the east.
A monk asked Master Jiufeng Qin, "What is the meaning of the West? He replied, "A single inch of tortoise hair weighs nine pounds."
Ordinarily silent when not meeting anyone, speaking immediately wounds the truth as if being too intimate;
disregarding the phoenixes resting within the fire, it startles the stone tiger to secretly give rise to anger.
A monk asked Linji, "What is the 'blow-off hair sword'? Linji said, "A disaster! A disaster! The monk bowed, and Linji struck him.

The sword hidden in its scabbard is cold and makes one shiver with chill; if you intend to ask further, you will linger and pass beyond the southern peaks, yet still desire to press forward while seeking retreat.
Afterwards, a wind of sorrow circled the mountain stream for a thousand ages.
A monk asked Daisui, "What is the lamp within the room? He replied, "Three people testify that a tortoise becomes a turtle."
When six ears conspire together, the matter can be accomplished; only through direct speech does one manifest their true heart. Who comes to stir the lamp-flame within the chamber?
A white-haired child with fresh hair at both temples.
A monk asked Ruiyan, "What is the Prince at Birth? Ruiyan said: "He cannot be led out from the deep palace;
his noble and extraordinary nature has its own appointed time. Few can accompany him through the spring gardens of the six palaces. At midnight, the stars cluster as the celestial wheel revolves;
at dawn, the eastern enclosure is bright while the curtains hang still."
A monk asked Master Wenshu of Dingzhou, "What was the meaning of the ancients hanging down one foot?
He replied, "Sitting for long becomes weary.
"The letter has just been sent, yet it is already in haste; Hanging down one foot, he follows in the footsteps of the ancients. Who understands that sitting for long becomes weary?"
All. Like snow falling on a red furnace, they naturally commune with one another.
A monk asked Master Shanglan Chao, "After Sudhana saw Mañjuśrī, why did he then travel to the south?
Lan said, "Learning depends on entering the room; knowledge leads to mastery of all quarters. The monk asked, "Upon reaching the city of Sumāgadhā, why..."
Then Maitreya sent him to see Mañjuśrī, who said: "The Way is boundless and vast; it never ceases upon meeting anyone.

The sun rises into the sky, high and low, its light reaching everywhere. The source of the Kunlun mountains flows into the rivers and streams. Clouds linger upon the spring mountains while the wind is inexhaustible;
The wild geese fly south as heaven and earth turn autumnal."
A monk asked Luopu, "What is that which cannot be contained within the Great Canon? Luopu said, "The rain nourishes the three types of grasses;
a single piece of jade shines by its very nature."
The *piṇḍapātra* rock flowers wear spring upon their brows at dawn; fragrant breezes occasionally gather atop the peaks of Vulture Mountain (*Gṛdhrakūṭa*).
You should know that within the jade elephant’s vase stands a stupa, possessing a lamp that uniquely illuminates heaven and earth.
A monk asked Master Baizhang Qing: "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? Baizhang said: "First, you must not ask;
second, you must not rest. The monk said: "I do not understand. Baizhang said: "When you come for a third time, I will meet with you."
Cease asking about Vimalakīrti lying ill in the city; at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, the empty space itself obscures the passage of time. There is no difficulty whatsoever in crossing the shifting sands;
do not listen to the warbling of the oriole in that forest.
A monk asked Master Bāzhuo Che, "If there is a person who neither abandons birth-and-death nor realizes nirvana, does the Master still take them up and carry them along?
Che said, "I do not. The monk asked, "Why do you not take them up and carry them along?
Che said, "This old monk roughly recognizes what is good and what is evil."
A child of a hundred years comes out of the gate; his entire body is crimson and raw, covered in dust and grime. He walks with ease through the midst of fire upon a cool ground;
those who recognize this would not dare to approach him.
A monk asked Tianpeng, "What is the Buddha? He replied: "Intimate and close, not leaving home; silent and still, not facing the door.
White clouds occasionally reflect the old mountain's green; bamboo locks thin mist, revealing several stalks. In the empty chamber, the night is cold and the autumn moon hangs far;
the wild geese return, heard from afar at the third watch."
A monk asked Heishan, "I do not ask about 'this very mind is Buddha. How is it that 'neither mind nor Buddha'?
Heishan said, "Know how to beat the drum.
Where the cloth-hair was raised, people exhausted themselves with words; how can this compare to the transmission of Heishan’s single phrase? One beat of the drum resounds through the universe.
In the vast expanse, where ice-cold waters reach a thousand fathoms, a lotus suddenly blooms.
A monk asked Master Huanglian, "What is the single phrase prior to sound? Huanglian replied, "There is no phrase prior to sound."
After the sound, one asks about what is yet to come;
before the sound, there are no words in the vast path of the empty kalpa. It is difficult for those who believe to find a phrase prior to the sound.
If you wish to exhaustively fathom the melody of the Canglang and white clouds, first look at the stone man revealing half his face.
A monk asked Master Bao of Zifú in Jízhōu, “What is the ancient song? Fú drew two circles facing each other.
“One tune, two tunes, played deep in the night; The pine wind and rain pass over the mountain before us. How pitiable is the Bǎn jade, separated from the state of Jīng!”
Xu. "Who is the one who knows this sound? Take it back.
A monk asked Master Zhi of Chongfu in Yizhou, "What are words of vast expansiveness? Zhi said, "The person without a tongue can speak them."
Speaking with broad and expansive words, he does not transgress the tongue; pure wind and lofty tones drift amidst slanting azure clouds.
The stone man greedily discusses the affairs of the western peak, unaware that mist is rising from the eastern crag to shroud him.
Master Dayang Ming’an asked Liangshan, “What is the formless site of enlightenment?
Liangshan pointed to Guanyin and said, “This was painted by the scholar Wu. As Yang was about to offer a response, Liangshan hurriedly called out, “This one has form.
What is the formless one? Upon hearing this, Yang attained realization beneath the words; he prostrated himself and returned to his quarters.
Yang stood his ground. Yangshan asked, "Why do you not speak a single phrase? Yang said, "I would not decline to speak, but I fear it would only take up paper and ink.
Yangshan laughed heartily and said, "These words shall be carved upon stone. Later, they were indeed inscribed upon a monument.

The Master took up the point and said: "The Way is vast throughout antiquity and the present; those who would travel it find it difficult to cross. The mountain is perilous and the precipices are steep; those who would ascend have no means of entry.
If one does not inquire into the traces left by predecessors, there will be no time to tread the path and attain entry. Thus, awakening arises from oneself, yet the seal must rely upon the teacher.
Through successive generations providing testimony, the life-span of the Buddha is sustained. This is the power of asking the way at the edge of a desolate cliff."
All traces have been exhausted; the cliff face has no door, and one’s strength is spent in advancing or retreating.
Now that the golden dragon has lost its water and the garuḍa has lifted it with its claws, it passes through the waves and surges anew to return to its original station.

O worthy ones, at this very moment, do you know where the ancients withdrew their positions? If you can know this, it may be said that ten-thousand-fathom peaks are hemmed in and a thousand waves are brought to a boil.

The dragon palaces and celestial realms share the same eaves; the phoenix pavilions and the stars blend their colors. The auspicious pines on the crags enshroud the valley, and the mists and fragrant grasses of the river permeate the air.
Unassailable by the gates of transformation, the thousand mountains rise far beyond. If one does not know where it falls, the crags are vast and no one asks;
when the dragon reaches the deep blue sea, it is profound indeed.

The path ended at a precipitous cliff; I questioned an old mountain man. He pointed elsewhere, saying the ridge to the west of the crag was closer than the east. As I prepared to advance, mist hung down and the mountain colors grew heavy;
looking back, I saw the sun glowing red atop the peak.
A monk asked Baizhang about a marvelous matter:
"Black winds blow, the ocean waves surge high; Thunder rolls through the void, roaring over the night tides. Faintly, fishing lamps hide along the ancient shore;
One oar cutting through the current—how could this be in vain?"
Once, while Master Lijun was brewing tea, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master held up his tea scoop. The monk said, "Is this not it? The Master threw it into the fire.

While the tea is still being brewed, someone comes to inquire; pick it up and present it clearly to him. If you encounter one with the hand that gathers the swallows at such a critical moment, your very life will be in peril—what can you do?
A monk asked Master Wenshu, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; to what place does the One return? He replied, "The Yellow River has nine bends.
The monk asked, "When the inquiry into the Dharma reaches its ultimate cause, where does it return? He replied, "The Yellow River flows through the billowing waves of the blue-green waters.
"You must know that atop the thousand peaks beyond the clouds, there stands a distinct, numinous pine tree, cold with the clinging dew."
While Xuefeng was serving as the kitchen steward at Dongshan, he was washing rice. Dongshan asked him, "Are you washing away the sand to keep the rice, or washing away the rice to keep the sand?
(The commentary says: *The shadowless cassia tree grows forever; through frost, it frequently bears fruit.*) Xuefeng replied, "I wash away the sand and the rice together.
Dongshan said, "What will the assembly eat then? (The commentary says: *The golden phoenix probes for fragrance.*)
The jade chicks eat the flower stamens and leaves, ever fresh and new. Feng then overturned the basin. Shan said, "You have indeed attained it;
however, you must go see another person before you have truly attained it. Later, he indeed succeeded to Deshan.
The alms bowl is filled, yet not a single thing is there; how could it compare to the precious ghee transformed at Gandhavyūha? The sun and moon, along with the celestial wheel, never shine upon it;
a wooden man dances his sleeves before the red furnace.
One day, Deshan ascended the hall and said, "To ask is to have a fault; not to ask is likewise deviant.
At that moment, a monk stepped forward and bowed. Deshan struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; why did you strike me?
Deshan replied, "What would it avail you to wait until you open your mouth?"
The Master took up the case and said: "Indeed, disaster arises from oneself; one harms others. The fire breaks out from within; its flames overturn the forest beasts.
Since he was playing with cleverness on a precipice, he could only have been pushed off. Hongyan let him go and let him pass through, yet it resulted in his being struck by misfortune in return.
Although he gained a small advantage, do you know that Deshan made a great mistake? If you can know this, then Deshan..."
The mountains shatter into dust. If you do not know how to attain it, even your discernment remains insufficient.
The golden wheel stirs slightly, its roar shaking heaven and earth; if one slightly opposes the golden body, one lies prostrate upon the grass.
Should one wish further to speak and come forward with a question, the wind of sorrow blows everything away, leaving all four neighbors utterly desolate.
A monk asked Xinghua, "What is it like when the military banners move with great urgency? Xinghua said: "Daily ration of half a catty of rice;

Leaving the city for another tower, one grieves in the dark. The moon sets and the stars divide as one follows the horse's hooves; The wind sweeps away the morning frost as the forest trees stretch far.
Deep in the night, a faint fire glows upon the marshy bank."
A monk asked Changqing, "How can one attain freedom from doubt? The Master extended his hand.
At the moment he extended his hand, ten-thousand-fathom cliffs crumbled; the withered river had no water, and the moon did not come. If you still harbor doubts, ask Pang Jushi another question:
"The stone woman and Huangmei—whom do they accompany?"
A monk asked Dongshan, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? Dongshan said, "After the fire, a single stalk of thatch;
when the wild fire burns it, it becomes ever more fresh. To this day, its smoke and flames cannot be quenched by rain; red lotuses on dry land shade the sun."
The Moon: A rootless tree grows lush green foliage into shade.
When the National Teacher called his attendant three times, he spoke;
when the National Teacher called the attendant, the words were not to be swallowed. His ears were not deaf, yet he had no way to clear himself.
One day, Master Youqi struck the bell and ascended the hall. As soon as the assembly had gathered, Youqi asked, "Who struck the bell?
A monk replied, "The Rector. Youqi said, "Come forward. When the monk stepped forward, Youqi struck him and then returned to his quarters to lie down.
Meeting by chance on the road, he asks for an explanation; do not hastily offer your heart’s response.
Though one may entrust a heavy burden to another to carry, it remains a matter of shame and secret embarrassment.
A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the Buddha? Dongshan replied, "Three pounds of flax.

One year in three years, everyone knows there is an intercalary month; yet there are those who are coarse and fail to keep track of the time. Last night the wild geese returned as the desert passes grew cold;
a piercing wind blew, causing the branches of the moonlit trees to burst open.
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? Yunmen said, "Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper.
"The peak of the Southern Mountain is high, the peak of the Northern Mountain is low; The traveler weeps with tears, hesitating at both ends. Last night the Fire Star moved into Ox and Dipper;
It shines upon those in the Western Jambudvīpa, yet they do not know it."
A monk asked Fengxue, "What is the Way? Fengxue said, "Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
The monk asked, "What is one who is on the Way? Fengxue said, "Ask the city magistrate."
The Master took up the case and said: "Thus it is said that the Way depends on the person; its practice lies with oneself. When a question reaches its ultimate limit, awakening is resolved;
when an answer is given, the fundamental principle is upheld. It is not that people labor in vain as they advance. Why? Because the single path above, where all sages do not travel, remains."
In the mere interval of deliberation, one loses one’s body and life. For this reason, auspicious omens are welcomed at the Dragon Pavilion, and the Purple Hall is shrouded in mist.
Moss overgrows the stone steps; incense smoke rises as the people fall silent. At such a moment as this, would you permit yourself even a breath?
If there were even the space for a single breath, it would be ten thousand miles along the long road.

The deep inner palace and forbidden halls are shielded by layered enclosures; the eaves are still, and purple qi hangs from the pillars. Moss covers the ground, blocking access to the court for audiences;
let those of the household point the way, and do not hesitate.
Citing the story of Yangshan planting his spade:
Where Muzhou asked, few understood; he answered him by planting it in the ground, drowning out the patriarchs and Buddhas.
Xuansha stepped on it and refused to acknowledge it by his side, sparing the lush greenery from being weighed down by the depth of spring.
A monk asked Fayan, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "You are Huichao.
When traveling over treacherous paths, it is difficult to ask for the way; someone may point toward the north village or the south.
Though countless people come and go through Chang'an, how many can pass the pass without their bells jingling?
